reading.body:
The Independent Community Bankers of America filed 8 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI, naming 21 lobbyists and two bills, HR 2152 and S 2296.

The pattern is concentration. Eight filings carry the whole record, and the same names recur across them: twelve lobbyists appear on all 8, three on 6, three on 4, and three on 2 or fewer. This is a trade association deploying a standing roster rather than assembling a team per issue. The two named bills are the only legislative targets the data identifies.

For AI specifically, the relevant fact is who is at the table. Community banks are not frontier model developers and do not buy hyperscale compute. Their interest in AI runs through lending, fraud detection, and compliance, which means the lobbying here is about how AI rules apply to small institutions rather than about building capacity. That is a different pressure point on the same regulatory surface that larger AI legislation touches.

What the data does not say is what the ICBA argued. A filing reports that a firm lobbied on an issue, not the position taken, so the direction of the advocacy is unknown. The data also does not cover spending amounts, agency contacts, or any AI activity by this client outside these 8 filings.

summary: INDEPENDENT COMMUNITY BANKERS OF AMERICA filed 8 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 19194.
